title: Meeting Floyd Turner and Seattle musicians
summary: On layovers in Seattle Joe sat in with the Turner family orchestra and other Chicago players.

bands.name: Edith Turner and the Jazz Giants

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: From that boat is that where you got into your Seattle period?
That's right. When we hit Seattle, like I said, we had the night off. We would dock about 7 o'clock

in the morning. We left San Francisco on the Tuesday, and we got to Seattle on like a Saturday morning -- a Friday or Saturday, I can't think. It was a fast boat; it went over 32 knots an hour. Anyway, we had that time off. So what's a musician going to do? Look for some liquor and a bootlegging joint in those days....
That's right, and have a session. That's the first time I met Floyd Turner.
Up there. They had the family orchestra.
Edith Turner and the Jazz Giants, or whatever it was called.

That's right. Her and her husband. She played piano and he played drums, and Floyd and them was young. I think they had one sister that danced... And they had a pretty good act on the Orpheum Circuit at one time.
Didn't he have a brother, too, Earl? Or was that his sister's husband maybe...?
Oh, I can't think of his sister's name offhand. Daisy? No, not Daisy; that was his wife. But whatever. Then did they... Did she ever kind of sign(?) up, or were they just another band up there?

Well, they was pretty popular in Seattle. They had... Yeah, they had a couple of pretty good bands. They had a guy out of Chicago named Oscar Hollins(?) that played clarinet and piano that was pretty good, and another guy from Chicago named Bill Hoy(?) played drums. Some other names will come to me.
